claims.text: Untreated CoCrFeNi has a comparatively coarse-grained near-surface structure.
The untreated CoCrFeNi near-surface structure degrades during high-temperature sliding.
A surface severe-plastic-deformation treatment can cause dynamic amorphization.
A surface severe-plastic-deformation treatment can produce an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The proposed treatment will form a partially amorphized, ultra-nanocrystalline layer on CoCrFeNi.
Refining the surface into the inverse Hall–Petch regime decreases its shear strength.
Formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer is linked to low friction and high wear resistance.
The refined layer will resist thermal degradation by maintaining a stable microstructure up to 800 °C.
The refined surface will provide continuous self-lubrication from room temperature to 800 °C.
The refined surface will prevent coarse-grain growth during sliding.
The refined surface will prevent oxidation-related degradation in air.
Treated CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
Treated CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
The beneficial ultra-nanocrystalline layer will remain intact during high-temperature sliding.
Untreated CoCrFeNi exhibits increased friction at elevated temperatures because of coarse grains and oxidation-related degradation.
Untreated CoCrFeNi exhibits increased wear at elevated temperatures because of coarse grains and oxidation-related degradation.
The intervention is anticipated to remain effective under loads similar to those used in prior tribological tests.
